inputs.original_text: The telling point in Bloomberg’s account is the divide between outside critics and the Israeli public: while people around the world focus on rising energy prices, canceled flights and the war’s costs, Israelis strongly support seeing it through. Those closest to the danger may understand better than distant commentators why security and national resolve cannot simply be set aside because a conflict is costly or unpopular abroad.
inputs.modified_text: The important point is that Israelis, who live with the danger, strongly support seeing the war through despite the costs. People abroad can focus on energy prices and canceled flights, but a nation’s first duty is the security of its people—not winning approval from distant critics. Resolve and continuity matter when a country’s safety is at stake.
